content: 1. Fentanyl and CYP3A4 Inhibitors: If co-administration of fentanyl with CYP3A4 inhibitors is necessary, monitor patients closely for respiratory depression and sedation. Adjust the fentanyl dose as needed until stable effects are achieved. 2. Tetracycline and CYP3A4 Inhibitors: Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4, such as fentanyl (transdermal and transmucosal), by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs when possible. 3. Ferric Maltol and Tetracycline: Ferric maltol decreases tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Ferrous Fumarate, Gluconate, and Sulfate with Tetracycline: These iron supplements reduce tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Fexinidazole and Tetracycline: Fexinidazole increases tetracycline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor for adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 6. Tetracycline and Finerenone: Tetracycline increases finerenone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor serum potassium during therapy initiation and dosage adjustments. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 7. Tetracycline and Flibanserin: Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. Flibanserin with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 8. Tetracycline and Fondaparinux: Tetracycline may increase the effects of fondaparinux through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance is unknown. 9. Fosphenytoin and Tetracycline: Fosphenytoin decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Tetracycline and Gepirone: Tetracycline increases gepirone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce gepirone dose by 50% when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 11. Tetracycline and Heparin: Tetracycline may increase the effects of heparin through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance is unknown. 12. Idelalisib and Tetracycline: Idelalisib increases tetracycline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 13. Tetracycline and Ifosfamide: Tetracycline decreases ifosfamide effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Iloperidone and Tetracycline: Iloperidone increases tetracycline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Tetracycline and Infigratinib: Tetracycline increases infigratinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 16. Tetracycline and Irinotecan (including liposomal): Tetracycline increases irinotecan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 17. Iron Supplements (e.g., Iron Dextran, Iron Sucrose) and Tetracycline: These reduce tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 18. Lanthanum Carbonate and Tetracycline: Lanthanum carbonate decreases tetracycline levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer tetracycline at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum. 19. Larotrectinib and Tetracycline: Larotrectinib increases tetracycline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 20. Tetracycline and Lefamulin: Tetracycline increases lefamulin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 21. Tetracycline and Lemborexant: Tetracycline increases lemborexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 22. Lenacapavir and Tetracycline: Lenacapavir increases tetracycline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for adverse reactions. 23. Tetracycline and Levamlodipine: Tetracycline increases levamlodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema. Dose reduction may be required. 24. Levofloxacin and Tetracycline: Levofloxacin increases tetracycline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 25. Tetracycline and Levonorgestrel/Ethinyl Estradiol: Tetracycline decreases the effectiveness of oral contraceptives by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low but should be monitored. 26. Tetracycline and Lomitapide: Co-administration is contraindicated as tetracycline significantly increases lomitapide levels. 27. Tetracycline and Lonafarnib: Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of significant drug interactions with CYP3A4 inhibitors. 28. Lorlatinib and Tetracycline: Lorlatinib decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 29. Tetracycline and Lumateperone: Tetracycline increases lumateperone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 30. Tetracycline and Lurbinectedin: Tetracycline increases lurbinectedin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 31. Magnesium Salts (e.g., Magnesium Chloride, Citrate, Hydroxide, Oxide, Sulfate) and Tetracycline: These reduce tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer magnesium 2 hours before or 4 hours after tetracycline. 32. Tetracycline and Mavacamten: Tetracycline increases mavacamten levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments may be required. 33. Tetracycline and Mavorixafor: Tetracycline increases mavorixafor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects and adjust the dose if necessary. 34. Tetracycline and Mefloquine: Tetracycline increases mefloquine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 35. Tetracycline and Mestranol: Tetracycline decreases mestranol levels by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low but should be monitored. 36. Tetracycline and Methotrexate: Tetracycline increases methotrexate levels by decreasing its elimination. Monitor methotrexate plasma concentrations and signs of toxicity. 37. Tetracycline and Methoxsalen: Co-administration increases the risk of toxicity due to additive photosensitizing effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Tetracycline and Methoxyflurane: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 39. Tetracycline and Methyl Aminolevulinate: Co-administration increases photosensitizing effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 40. Tetracycline and Microbiota Oral: Tetracycline decreases the efficacy of microbiota oral therapy. Complete antibiotic regimens 2-4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. 41. Tetracycline and Midazolam (Intranasal): Tetracycline increases midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 42. Tetracycline and Mipomersen: Both drugs may increase hepatic enzyme levels. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. 43. Mitotane and Tetracycline: Mitotane decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for dosage adjustments. 44. Nafcillin and Tetracycline: Nafcillin decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 45. Tetracycline and Naldemedine: Tetracycline increases naldemedine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects. 46. Tetracycline and Naloxegol: Tetracycline increases naloxegol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
